newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes higher at 1,010.85.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes higher at 1,010.85.

text.p: Colombia's peso extended its gains for the fourth consecutive trading session, ending up 4.1 pesos against the dollar at 1,010.85.

Interbank dealers attributed the rise to inflows of dollars from oil and coffee sales abroad, but they said banks had also entered the market to speculate based on widespread expectations that the peso will continue to strengthen in the weeks ahead.
Dealers reported 325 trades in Friday's session for a total of $1.21 million and said the peso held in a 1,015.10 to 1,009.65 range.
Friday's close was the highest since January 12 and dealers said the peso was expected to jump back up above the 1,000-to-one psychological barrier in trading next week.
The peso fell below the barrier for the first time on Jan. 4.

In addition to oil and coffee revenues, some analysts, including a commentator in the latest issue of Colombia's financial news magazine Dinero, say the peso's rise is due to a recent increase in the bulk smuggling of drug dollars into Colombia.
